verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs confirm notes are normally stored as local Markdown files and can be exported to Markdown, JSON, EDN, OPML, and HTML (logseq-docs-8, logseq-docs-30), which is real evidence for open-format ownership. However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict the durability of this claim: users note the exported Markdown isn't standard-compatible with other Markdown tools due to non-standard spacing (logseq-comm-19), and that Logseq's new DB-based version moves away from keeping all data as plain Markdown files, undermining the 'outlives the vendor' guarantee (logseq-comm-14, logseq-comm-9). Missing for 10: independent verification that exported files are fully portable/standard, and clarity on whether the DB version retains a markdown/JSON escape hatch.
